jobs.title: Manager, Product Manager
jobs.jd_full:
Canonical is a leading provider of open source software and operating systems to the global enterprise and technology markets. Our platform, Ubuntu, is very widely used in breakthrough enterprise initiatives such as public cloud, data science, AI, engineering innovation and IoT. Our customers include the world's leading public cloud and silicon providers, and industry leaders in many sectors. The company is a pioneer of global distributed collaboration, with 1200+ colleagues in 75+ countries and very few office based roles. Teams meet two to four times yearly in person, in interesting locations around the world, to align on strategy and execution.

The company is founder led, profitable and growing.

Canonical’s product management team are technologists who have a passion for delivering products and solutions that help shape market demands while elevating open source software everywhere. This is a general application track for the product management positions at Canonical, across all levels of team leads. As a manager, you will lead a team of product managers, mentoring them to ensure their success while driving alignment with company goals. You will set a clear vision, prioritize work effectively, and ensure the team delivers high-quality products that meet business and user needs. Apply here if you excel at leadership, communication, and technical vision, and believe you can drive product strategy for the business needs of tomorrow. During the interview process we will identify specific software products which would be a good fit for your interests.

We believe that open source is transforming the way that enterprises solve their business needs. Although open source has been around for thirty years, it is only now fundamental to every corner of the software landscape. Going forward we believe open source will have an even bigger impact as it moves into specialised vertical markets. Our goal is to make open source easier, more reliable and more secure for deployment and development. We strive to be the provider of ‘most software to most companies’, starting with Ubuntu but expanding to cover every class of application on every class of compute. To deliver on that ambition, we select product managers for their intellect and strong drive to advance the open source community. Together, we aim to improve open source quality, outreach, and impact. Our product managers set the vision and the direction to ensure teams deliver the right products in the right markets at the right time. They push the boundaries of the technology landscape to identify and deliver products into new and existing market opportunities.

Our product managers are technology professionals with a software engineering background who strive to become business executives and entrepreneurs. We discuss strategy, plan product development, drive engagement, and promote the open source way. We oversee the entire product lifecycle from conception to delivery, blending technical expertise, strategic thinking, analytics, project management skills and effective communication to ensure products meet both user needs and business objectives.

We have open product manager roles across a wide range of product domains, including:

  • Ubuntu Platform - Our Ubuntu experience on Desktop, Server, Windows (WSL), Multipass, Gaming, Enterprise, & Hardware Enablement
  • Ubuntu Pro Services - Our key commercial offerings Ubuntu Pro, Compliance, Standards, Security Engineering, and Managed Services on cloud and on prem
  • IoT - Ubuntu on embedded devices and/or edge servers, device management, and robotics
  • Cloud - Ubuntu in public and private clouds, promoting automation frameworks, and including technologies such as Kubernetes, MAAS, and LXD
  • Telco - Open source for Telco's including technologies and standards related to Core Network, RAN/vRAN, SoNIC, DENT, and SmartNICs
  • Finance - Open source solutions for financial institutions including trading platforms, blockchain technologies, regulatory compliance, and AI-driven analytics
  • Automotive - Open source solutions for autonomous driving, in-vehicle infotainment, connected vehicles, and compliance with automotive industry standards such as ISO 26262 and ISO 21434
  • Application Management - Open source solutions in the enterprise including Observability, IAM, App Stores and technologies such Grafana, GitOps, and Juju Charms

If your domain of expertise isn’t listed above, yet you feel it’s relevant to Canonical, then feel free to apply anyway. We will route you to the most suitable team.

Location: These roles are home based in the EMEA time zone.

This role entails

  • Lead the product development lifecycle, reviewing the priorities and goals for your product
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams such as engineering, design, marketing, and sales
  • Address common challenges across projects, align on priorities, enable informed decisions, and keep business execution on track
  • Conduct market research, analyse industry trends, and gather customer feedback to identify opportunities
  • Communicate your product vision, status updates, and key decisions to ensure alignment and manage expectations
  • Conduct usability testing, analyse user feedback, and iterate on the product to improve the user experience
  • Collaborate with marketing, sales, and support teams to develop go-to-market strategies, create product documentation, and provide training
  • Contribute to the success of our sales team in winning new opportunities, reviewing customer feedback and participating in customer meetings
  • Guide and mentor a team of product managers, helping them grow in their roles and succeed in their projects
  • Oversee the work of multiple product lines, ensuring consistency in strategy and execution across your team
  • Facilitate collaboration and resolve conflicts within your team and across other departments

What we are looking for in you

  • Exceptional academic results at high school and university
  • Understanding of Linux and the wider open source software community
  • Understanding of computer architecture, application development, datacenters, cloud or devices
  • Passion to write about technologies and the tech landscape
  • A strong work ethic, and personal interests aligned with the open source movement
  • Curiosity, and the habit of continuous learning
  • A strong sense of ownership
  • Problem solving and the ability to innovate
  • Outstanding communications skills in English, both verbal and written
  • For more senior positions, product management experience in the software industry
  • Proven experience in managing and mentoring product managers or cross-functional teams
  • Ability to manage multiple projects or product lines while maintaining focus on key priorities
  • Demonstrated leadership in aligning diverse teams and driving consensus around product strategies
  • Willingness to travel internationally up to 4 times a year for company events up to two weeks long

Additional skills that we value

  • Familiarity with a particular verticals (e.g. Telco, Finance, Industrial, Automotive)
  • Familiarity with the technology ecosystem including Silicon, IHV, ISV, ODM/OEMs, cloud service providers and channel
  • Familiarity with cloud native technologies such as Kubernetes, Docker containers & Snaps
  • Familiarity with embedded and connected device technology and ecosystems
  • Experience in managing distributed teams across different time zones
  • Demonstrated ability to foster collaboration and innovation in team settings

What we offer colleagues

We consider geographical location, experience, and performance in shaping compensation worldwide. We revisit compensation annually (and more often for graduates and associates) to ensure we recognise outstanding performance. In addition to base pay, we offer a performance-driven annual bonus or commission. We provide all team members with additional benefits, which reflect our values and ideals. We balance our programs to meet local needs and ensure fairness globally.

  • Distributed work environment with twice-yearly team sprints in person
  • Personal learning and development budget of USD 2,000 per year
  • Annual compensation review
  • Recognition rewards
  • Annual holiday leave
  • Maternity and paternity leave
  • Employee Assistance Program
  • Opportunity to travel to new locations to meet colleagues
  • Priority Pass, and travel upgrades for long haul company events

About Canonical

Canonical is a pioneering tech firm at the forefront of the global move to open source. As the company that publishes Ubuntu, one of the most important open source projects and the platform for AI, IoT and the cloud, we are changing the world of software. We recruit on a global basis and set a very high standard for people joining the company. We expect excellence - in order to succeed, we need to be the best at what we do. Most colleagues at Canonical have worked from home since its inception in 2004.​ Working here is a step into the future, and will challenge you to think differently, work smarter, learn new skills, and raise your game.

Canonical is an equal opportunity employer

We are proud to foster a workplace free from discrimination. Diversity of experience, perspectives, and background create a better work environment and better products. Whatever your identity, we will give your application fair consideration.

jobs.title: Business Applications Specialist (Order to Cash)
jobs.jd_full:
About Pleo

Messy spend management is tricky business. And tedious processes are a lose-lose situation for all involved, not just finance. At Pleo, we're changing that. We build spend solutions that make managing money seamless, empowering, and surprisingly effective for finance teams and employees alike - with a vision to help all businesses ‘go beyond’.

The word ‘Pleo’ actually means ‘more than you’d expect’, and living by that mantra has been the secret to our success over the last 10 years.

Now, we’re at a pivotal moment in our journey; every move we make has a direct impact on our 40,000+ customers, our business, and our collective success. We need people who take pride in uncovering customer needs, who turn complex problems into simple solutions, challenge the way things are done (respectfully), and always aim high. With great ambitions driving us forward, we can’t say we’ve got this whole thing figured out. And frankly, that’s half the fun! What we can say is that we’re a driven, progressive, and, importantly, a kind bunch of 850+ people from over 100 nationalities, all committed to delivering the future of business spending, together.

The role

Every deal Pleo closes runs through a chain of systems. It starts with a quote in the CRM, moves through pricing, contract, and billing, and ends with revenue in the ERP. You’ll own that chain.

This role is part systems specialist and part product owner. You’ll manage the Order-to-Cash application portfolio as a product. That means a clear roadmap, a prioritised backlog, and an honest view of what gets built and why. You’ll work with Billing, Deal Desk, Pricing, Finance, and Sales, who all want different things from the same systems. You’ll balance those needs and decide.

As Pleo moves upmarket, quoting and billing are getting more complex: multi-entity accounts, multiple currencies, and enterprise contracts. You’ll help shape the next generation of our quote-to-cash tooling.

What you’ll do

  • Own the O2C portfolio. Act as product owner for the tools that support quote to cash, including HubSpot Quoting, our pricing calculator and CPQ, DocuSign and integrations with Zuora, and NetSuite

  • Set the roadmap. Build and maintain a roadmap and backlog that reflect business priorities. Think 1–2 quarters ahead and propose improvements before they become problems.

  • Manage demand. Take in requests from O2C, Billing, Deal Desk, Pricing, and Sales. Assess impact, prioritise against revenue outcomes, and give stakeholders clear answers, including no.

  • Design end-to-end processes. Map the lead-to-cash flow, find breaks and manual workarounds, and design solutions that hold up at enterprise scale.

  • Deliver large changes. Lead medium and large enhancements from requirements through process flows, user stories, configuration, UAT, and release.

  • Work with engineers. Translate business needs into clear requirements for BAT Engineering, and own functional testing and sign-off.

  • Protect billing integrity. Make sure what’s sold, what’s contracted, and what’s billed stay in sync. Treat data quality, controls, and audit trails as part of the job.

  • Own vendor relationships. Manage key O2C vendors, including performance against SLAs, licence usage, and input into renewals with Procurement.

  • Support tooling decisions. Contribute to evaluations of off-the-shelf CPQ and CLM options, and to buy-versus-build decisions.

  • Enable and mentor. Train business users on new processes, peer review colleagues’ work, and support analysts on the team.

What you’ll bring

  • 8+ years in business applications, with deep experience across quote-to-cash or order-to-cash systems.

  • Hands-on experience with CPQ, billing, and ERP platforms, such as Zuora, NetSuite, Salesforce CPQ, HubSpot Quotes, Chargebee, or similar. You understand how they connect.

  • Solid knowledge of SaaS commercial processes, including pricing and packaging, discounting and approvals, contracts, subscription billing, invoicing, and revenue recognition basics.

  • Product ownership experience: roadmaps, backlogs, prioritisation frameworks, and saying no with a reason.

  • Strong stakeholder management. You can hold competing priorities from Finance, Sales, and Deal Desk in one conversation and get to a decision.

  • Experience leading delivery in Agile teams, including user stories, sprints, UAT, and release management.

  • Excellent written and spoken English. You’ll work with teams across Europe every day.

Nice to have

  • Experience implementing or migrating CPQ or CLM tools.

  • Experience with multi-entity, multi-currency billing in a regulated or fintech environment.

  • Familiarity with SQL or data tools for reconciliation and reporting.

Show me the benefits

  • Your own Pleo card (no more out-of-pocket spending!)

  • Lunch is on us for your work days - enjoy catered meals or receive a lunch allowance based on your local office

  • Comprehensive private healthcare - depending on your location, coverage options include Vitality, Alan or Médis

  • 25 days of annual leave + public holidays (additional days may apply in select countries based on local standards).

  • For our Team, we offer both hybrid and fully remote working options

  • We use MyndUp to give our employees access to free mental health and well-being support with great success so far

  • Paid parental leave - we want to make sure that we're supportive of families and help you feel that you don't have to compromise your family due to work

About your application

  • English first. Since it's our company language, please submit your application in English. You’ll be using it a lot if you join us.

  • A fair look for everyone. Our talent team reads every single application to ensure the process is fair. To keep things running smoothly, we only accept applications through our system—our support team can’t pass on calls or emails.

  • Diversity drives us. We can only reach our goals if our team reflects the world around us. That starts with you hitting apply, even if you don't tick every single box. We encourage people from all backgrounds and experiences to join us.

  • Interview at your best. We want you to feel comfortable throughout the process. If you have any accessibility requirements or need a specific format, email belonging@pleo.io. We’ll design a process that works for you.

  • Your data is safe. When you apply, we process your personal data as a data processor. For more information on how Pleo processes personal data, read our Privacy Policy here.

  • Applying for multiple roles? Nothing is stopping you, and we assess every role independently. However, we do look for alignment, so make sure you can explain why your interest and experience are right for each specific role.

  • Reapplying. If you’re applying for the same role again, please wait six months from your last decision before hitting submit.

jobs.title: Product Manager, Salesforce
jobs.jd_full:
About Kaseya

Kaseya is the leading provider of AI-powered IT management and cybersecurity software, serving Managed Service Providers (MSPs) and internal IT organizations worldwide. Our comprehensive platform helps organizations efficiently manage, secure, and automate their IT environments, driving operational efficiency and long-term business success.

Backed by Insight Partners, a leading global software investor, Kaseya has experienced sustained double-digit growth and continues to expand its global footprint. Today, Kaseya supports customers in more than 20 countries and manages over 15 million endpoints worldwide.

Founded in 2000, Kaseya was built by builders - and we're still building. We look for people who create rather than wait, who see a hard problem and lean in, and who treat challenges as raw material. At Kaseya, everyone plays a role in shaping the future of IT: whether you're in engineering, product, sales, marketing, customer support, or operations, your work helps protect, defend, and optimize IT environments across the globe.

We're building teams that grow, perform, and make an impact. If you're driven by the itch to make things better - a product, a process, a career - you'll fit right in.

At Kaseya, we don't just raise the bar. We build it.

Position Summary

Kaseya is seeking a strategic, detail-oriented Product Manager to join our Business Information Systems (BIS) team. This individual will drive the vision, roadmap, and execution of enterprise capabilities supporting our Product Business Systems (PBS), with a focus on product configuration, pricing, fulfillment, software provisioning, entitlements, usage, and overage management.

This role will support Kaseya’s current operating environment while helping shape the future-state architecture and processes needed to support continued growth and transformation. PBS capabilities span multiple platforms, including Salesforce, NetSuite, integrations, and Kaseya products such as Kaseya One. As Kaseya evolves its enterprise systems landscape, this individual will help guide the transition toward a scalable architecture anchored by Salesforce Revenue Cloud Advanced (RCA), Salesforce Commerce Cloud, Oracle ERP, and related applications.

The ideal candidate brings a strong understanding of the Lead-to-Cash lifecycle within an enterprise SaaS environment, including product and pricing configuration, bundle management, software license provisioning, entitlement management, and usage-based billing. This person must be comfortable navigating complex integrations, balancing competing priorities, and partnering across business and technical teams to simplify legacy processes, strengthen controls, and deliver scalable solutions.

Key Responsibilities

  • Product Strategy and Roadmap: Define and manage the product roadmap for Product and Pricing, Fulfillment, and Provisioning capabilities, ensuring alignment with corporate strategy, revenue operations priorities, finance transformation goals, customer experience improvements, and future-state migration objectives.
  • Product and Pricing Management: Lead capabilities related to product configuration, catalog management, SKU creation, product hierarchies, master data governance, pricing models, discount management, renewal pricing, promotions, and bundle configuration.
  • Fulfillment and Provisioning: Drive requirements and solutions for automated, manual, and hybrid provisioning models, fulfillment routing, tenant and instance creation, customer-to-tenant mapping, license provisioning, and entitlement lifecycle management.
  • Lead-to-Cash Lifecycle: Lead requirements definition and solution alignment across the Lead-to-Cash lifecycle, including product and pricing setup, order fulfillment, provisioning, usage capture, overage management, billing, revenue recognition, and reporting.
  • Product Ownership and Agile Delivery: Own and manage the product backlog, develop clear user stories and acceptance criteria, and lead backlog refinement, sprint planning, discovery sessions, solution reviews, demonstrations, and other Agile ceremonies.
  • Systems and Integration Management: Serve as a subject matter expert across current and future-state platforms, including Salesforce, Salesforce Revenue Cloud Advanced, NetSuite, Oracle ERP, MuleSoft, Oracle Integration Cloud (OIC), Kaseya One, and related applications. Partner with technical teams to ensure reliable integrations and consistent data flows.
  • Cross-Functional Collaboration: Partner with Finance, Billing Operations, Revenue Operations, Sales Operations, Customer Operations, Product, Engineering, Enterprise Architecture, Security, and IT to gather requirements, prioritize initiatives, resolve issues, and deliver scalable business outcomes.
  • Business Process Optimization: Identify opportunities to simplify workflows, reduce manual intervention, clarify ownership, improve operational handoffs, strengthen governance, and increase automation across PBS capabilities.
  • Transformation and Migration Readiness: Balance support for legacy systems with future-state transformation priorities, ensuring legacy enhancements deliver measurable value, reduce operational risk, or improve migration readiness.
  • Governance, Risk, and Compliance: Ensure solutions align with enterprise policies, internal controls, data privacy, and security requirements. Maintain clear documentation of requirements, business rules, integration dependencies, decisions, testing coverage, and operational readiness.
  • Continuous Improvement: Monitor system performance, user adoption, data quality, defect trends, billing accuracy, provisioning effectiveness, and operational outcomes to identify opportunities for improvement and scalability.
  • Delivery and Stakeholder Alignment: Partner with Engineering Leads, QA, Scrum Masters, Business Process Leads, and Release/PMO teams to manage dependencies, remove blockers, coordinate testing, and deliver capabilities aligned with business objectives and release milestones.

Required Qualifications

  • 7+ years of experience in product management, product ownership, business systems analysis, CRM systems, revenue operations systems, or enterprise solution delivery.
  • Proven experience with Lead-to-Cash, Quote-to-Cash, or subscription lifecycle processes within an enterprise SaaS environment.
  • Strong working knowledge of Salesforce CPQ, Salesforce Revenue Cloud, Revenue Cloud Advanced, or comparable enterprise product configuration and pricing platforms.
  • Experience with product catalog management, SKU management, pricing configuration, discounting, bundle management, or product master data governance.
  • Hands-on experience with software license provisioning, entitlement management, or fulfillment workflows, including integrations using platforms such as MuleSoft or Boomi.
  • Experience with usage-based pricing models, including usage capture, rating, overage management, and associated billing or revenue processes.
  • Understanding of integrated system flows across sales, order management, billing, accounts receivable, collections, revenue recognition, and reporting.
  • Demonstrated success managing cross-functional Agile delivery teams and driving complex enterprise initiatives from requirements through implementation.
  • Strong understanding of business process mapping, technical integrations, data dependencies, user stories, acceptance criteria, and system controls.
  • Excellent communication, stakeholder management, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to influence decisions and drive alignment across business and technical teams.
  • Ability to operate effectively in a fast-paced, evolving environment while balancing business-as-usual support, competing priorities, and future-state transformation initiatives.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with Salesforce Revenue Cloud Advanced (RCA), Salesforce Commerce Cloud, Oracle ERP, NetSuite, MuleSoft, or Oracle Integration Cloud (OIC).
  • Experience supporting enterprise SaaS subscription models, managed service providers (MSPs), usage-based billing, and customer lifecycle processes.
  • Familiarity with Kaseya One or comparable software provisioning, entitlement, and license management platforms.
  • Experience with revenue operations, billing operations, finance transformation, or enterprise business systems within a complex, integrated technology environment.
  • Experience supporting enterprise architecture modernization, legacy platform transitions, data governance initiatives, and large-scale systems migration.
  • Knowledge of revenue recognition and billing metadata requirements associated with product, pricing, usage, and subscription management.

jobs.title: Director, New Business Operations
jobs.jd_full:
Cloudinary is the Image and Video API platform trusted by millions of developers and over 10,000 companies worldwide. Our powerful tools fuel websites to be faster, richer in user engagement, and breakthrough creativity. With a growing suite of products that support everything from developer efficiency to brand storytelling, Cloudinary is becoming the visual layer of the web.

Cloudinary has a globally distributed team across North America, EMEA, and Asia-Pacific, united by a shared commitment to building smart, scalable technology and a culture rooted in humility, curiosity, and collaboration. At Cloudinary, we celebrate Life & Work. We believe in healthy growth, working with purpose, and creating meaningful value. If you’re looking for a place where your voice matters and your work truly makes an impact, this may be the opportunity for you.

Cloudinary is looking for a Director, New Business Operations to make our New Business organization more predictable, focused, and effective as we scale. You will own the operating system behind our New Business motions - the processes, data, cadence, and tools that help leaders and sellers turn pipeline into ARR.

Reporting to the VP, Revenue Operations & Enablement, you will be the operating partner to New Business leadership, Account Executives, and Sales Engineers. You will work cross-functionally with Marketing, Pricing, Finance, IT, Legal, Data, Enablement, and Channels & Alliances to improve how the business runs.

This role is ideal for a hands-on operator who combines sales-operations expertise, analytical judgment, cross-functional execution, and a high bar for clarity and adoption. You will build the systems and rhythms that make it easier to inspect performance, resolve blockers, and improve field execution without owning the sale itself.

Responsibilities:

• Own and evolve the operating model and cadence for all New Business motions, including standards, agendas, decision rights, and priorities.

• Lead forecast readiness and opportunity inspection, giving leaders an accurate, timely view of performance, risk, upside, stage progression, qualification, next steps, close dates, and opportunity health.

• Improve pipeline hygiene, opportunity completeness, and Salesforce data quality; combine Account Executive, Sales Engineer, and system signals to surface deal risk, blockers, and forecast changes early.

• Build and curate reporting that drives decisions, consolidating redundant dashboards into clear, useful views for New Business leaders and the field.

• Lead cross-functional initiatives involving CRM, CPQ, RFPs, pricing, and other GTM systems and processes from problem definition through delivery and adoption.

• Translate field needs into clear requirements, acceptance criteria, and success measures; coordinate owners, make tradeoffs visible, remove blockers, and escalate decisions with context.

• Partner with Marketing, Enablement, and Channels & Alliances to align handoffs and shared workflows, and convert field feedback into a prioritized improvement backlog.

• Create durable playbooks and inspection mechanisms; measure adoption, data quality, forecast accuracy, and process performance, and use the evidence to improve the operating model.

About You:

• Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical experience, plus 10+ years of progressive experience in Business Operations, Sales Strategy, or related roles in B2B SaaS or technology companies.

This role is accountable for completion. Community managers and Regional Vice Presidents (RVP) stay informed and partner on access and communication, but they are not responsible for completing the work. jobs.title: Staff Product Manager, Longitudinal Patient Record
jobs.jd_full:
At Counterpart Health, we are transforming healthcare and improving patient care with our innovative primary care tool, Counterpart Assistant. By supporting Primary Care Physicians (PCPs), we deliver improved outcomes at lower cost through early diagnosis and longitudinal care management of chronic conditions.

We’re hiring a Staff Product Manager to own the longitudinal patient record, one trusted view of the care each patient receives across every setting, from the primary care office to the specialist to a hospital stay. Every Counterpart product builds on this record.

Our clinical data comes from hundreds of sources, including health information exchanges, EHRs, labs, ADT feeds, pharmacy fills, prior authorizations, and claims from our health plan customers. Each one captures part of a patient’s care. The longitudinal record connects them into one history of the patient’s visits, conditions, medications, and results.

You will ensure completeness and consistency in how those sources come together, so providers walk into each visit with the full picture, care gaps get closed, and quality and risk adjustment programs capture the care patients actually received.

Our AI reasons over the same record, so improvements to the record expand what our AI can reliably do. That work takes clear clinical definitions, sound data modeling, and AI applied where it adds scale, such as classifying documents and connecting records across sources. The result is that every AI tool we build works from the same view of each patient.

You will report to the Director of Product, Clinical Data Products, and lead the Longitudinal Patient Record pod. You will partner closely with engineering, our clinical team, and data consumers across the company.

What you will own and improve

  • Product strategy. Set the vision and roadmap for the longitudinal record. Find the highest-value problems across the products and programs that depend on it, and make the trade-offs among completeness, accuracy, timeliness, and investment.
  • A trusted record. Define how care events and their dates, settings, providers, and facilities are represented consistently, and how medications, conditions, labs, and procedures connect to those events and to the patient’s history over time. Set clinically grounded rules for combining sources that each describe part of the same care, so every fact can be traced to the evidence behind it.
  • A unified record of acute events. One record of each hospitalization, ED and post-discharge care management built from multiple sources such as: ADT notifications, prior authorization and admission notices, facility claims, medical records (especially discharge documentation), and where the patient went at discharge. Anyone working with the patient sees the whole stay, from admission through discharge to the next setting of care.
  • Data for every use case. The record serves providers at the point of care and the programs that depend on complete care history: quality measurement (HEDIS), risk adjustment and RADV audits, payment integrity, and revenue operations. Providers, quality analysts, and operational teams all work from the same care history.
  • How every source becomes part of the record. You own patient matching, deduplication, normalization, and clinical terminology mapping, which turn raw data from each source into a trusted part of the patient’s record. Every new source runs through them, so improvements are built once and reused across products.
  • Adoption. A canonical field counts only when clinicians use it. You own the path from definition to adoption: requirements, a migration plan per use case, and retiring fragmented, duplicate versions of the same data.

What success looks like

  • The record gets more complete, accurate, and timely, and you can show it with numbers.
  • Products and programs adopt the shared record and retire their own versions of it.
  • New customers and markets reach a usable patient record with less time and less one-off work.
  • You can show what those gains changed downstream: more complete evidence for quality and risk adjustment, earlier visibility into admissions and care transitions, and fewer inconsistencies across products.
  • You run a clear decision process with clinical and engineering partners, and definitions are documented, adopted, and applied consistently.

You should get in touch if

  • You have 8+ years of product management experience, including owning a data platform, data model, or shared data product used by multiple teams.
  • You have set product strategy for a platform with many internal consumers and made the trade-offs that came with it.
  • You have deep working knowledge of healthcare data and the clinical utility: institutional and professional claims, clinical documents such as C-CDA, FHIR resources, ADT feeds, and lab data. You know what part of a patient’s care each covers and where the gaps are.
  • You have defined canonical or master data (patient, provider, facility, encounter, clinical concepts) and gotten other teams to adopt it.
  • You work in the data yourself: reviewing charts, investigating discrepancies, running analyses, and testing a definition against real records before it ships. You use AI to accelerate that work and know how to validate its output.
  • You have led cross-functional projects through influence, setting direction and driving delivery across engineering, clinical, and operations teams you don’t directly manage.
  • You can point to a time a data improvement you owned contributed to a business result, such as a clinical outcome otherwise missed, avoided patient abrasion through duplication of care, physician time savings not chasing portals, or similar impact.

Benefits Overview:
